chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Qasim al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

While the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was seated, with him was his son Muhammad. He said: 'O Muhammad, bring me a vessel of water.' So he brought it to him, and he poured it with his right hand onto his left hand, then said: 'Praise is to Allah who made water purifying and did not make it impure.'
Then he cleaned his private part and said: 'O Allah, fortify my private part and keep it chaste, and conceal my nakedness and prohibit it from the Fire.'
Then he inhaled water and said: 'O Allah, do not prohibit the scent of Paradise from me, and make me among those who smell its scent, its fragrance, and its blossoms.'
Then he rinsed his mouth and said: 'O Allah, cause my tongue to speak with Your remembrance, and make me among those with whom You are pleased.'
Then he washed his face and said: 'O Allah, whiten my face on the Day when faces are blackened, and do not blacken my face on the Day when faces are whitened.'
Then he washed his right hand and said: 'O Allah, give me my Book in my right hand and eternity in my left hand.'
Then he washed his left hand and said: 'O Allah, do not give me my Book in my left hand, nor make it tied to my neck, and I seek refuge in You from the pieces of the Fires.'
Then he wiped his head and said: 'O Allah, overwhelm me with Your mercy, Your blessings, and Your forgiveness.'
Then he wiped upon his feet and said: 'O Allah, firm my feet upon the Bridge on the Day when feet waver, and make my striving in what pleases You about me.'

Then he turned to Muhammad and said: 'O Muhammad, whoever performs ablution like my ablution and says what I said, Allah creates for him an angel from every drop, which glorifies Him, exalts Him, proclaims His greatness, and testifies to His oneness, and records for him the reward of that.'

key_terms.الاسْتِنْجَاء: Cleaning the private parts with water
key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications recited during each step of Shia ritual ablution (wudu)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) practice of teaching Ali the specific supplications for each limb during ablution, a tradition emphasized in Shia jurisprudence as recommended (mustahabb) acts that elevate the ritual beyond mere physical cleansing. The promise of angels being created from each drop underscores the metaphysical significance of wudu, linking bodily purification with spiritual elevation and divine recording of deeds. This narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding the interplay between physical action and spiritual intention in Shia devotional practice.
